summary: We know from the Toronto Police Hate Crime Unit that the Jewish community was the most frequently victimized group in 2020. Anti-Semitic attacks have continued in 2021 with an extremely troubling rise in recent weeks and months. We have heard the valid concerns of the Jewish community and we stand with them against this hatred. The Jewish community is one that includes survivors of the Holocaust and their descendants – they know all too well the danger of anti-Semitism and the tragedies that follow when it is allowed to stand unchallenged. That is why we are committed as a City to confronting anti-Semitism – in all its forms - and ensuring Toronto Police are supported in the pursuit of hate crimes. We will not let hatred take root in our City and we will not let it grow. This is why our Toronto For All public education initiative this year will target anti-Semitism and why we have worked to put in place policies to stop hate rallies in our City. While we all have more work to do in the weeks, months, and years ahead to continue to confront anti-Semitism, it is important to the Jewish Community and to our entire City to send a clear message reaffirming that there is no place for any kind of attacks on the Jewish Community in Toronto. Along with a rise in incidents of anti-Semitism, we are also currently seeing a deeply concerning global increase in polarized discourse that…
decided: City Council on June 8 and 9, 2021, adopted the following: 1. City Council condemn in the strongest terms possible the recent acts of Anti-Semitism and hate and restate its commitment to an inclusive and welcoming City for all Toronto residents. 2. City Council express its support for a National Action Summit on Anti-Semitism with the participation of the Federal, Provincial and local governments. 3. City Council commit to relaunching the Toronto For All anti-Semitism campaign. 4. City Council direct the City Manager, in partnership with relevant divisions, to support Jewish community members on how to report hate-crimes.
